title: Partition-aware inflight limiter + graceful worker shutdown to reduce retry storms
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Our current worker topology uses a global semaphore for inflight request limits and a best-effort shutdown that waits for in-flight tasks with a static timeout. This has surfaced multiple forms of flakiness in high-throughput scenarios: partition hotspots lead to per-partition queueing and head-of-line blocking, global semaphores allow tenant A to starve tenant B, and abrupt shutdowns cause large retry storms (duplicate work + cascade failures).

Goal:
Replace the global inflight semaphore with a partition-aware token bucket limiter and implement a graceful shutdown handshake for both Redis and Kafka worker types such that:
- inflight capacity is enforced per-kafka-partition and per-redis-stream-consumer-group shard
- backpressure is signalled upstream (where possible) and shed gracefully otherwise
- shutdown is cooperative (drain + lease transfer) with a fallback timed drain to avoid long stalls
- migrate away from blocking Redis/Kafka client calls in hot paths to the async client APIs to eliminate blocking thread pool exhaustion

Scope/What we will deliver:
- new PartitionInflightLimiter component (token-bucket with jittered refill + soft/hard limits)
  - keys: kafka://<topic>#<partition> and redis://<stream>#<consumer-shard>
  - default soft limit 100, hard limit 150 per partition (configurable per-tenant)
  - metrics: limiter.current_tokens, limiter.soft_drop_count, limiter.hard_reject_count, limiter.wait_ms_p50/p95
- graceful shutdown protocol for workers
  - step 1: mark as DRAINING and stop pulling new messages from assigned partitions/streams
  - step 2: attempt in-place lease transfer (Kafka rebalance for consumer groups; Redis consumer group XCLAIM for stream ownership) within 5s
  - step 3: wait for inflight to drop below soft limit for up to 30s, then force-commit in-flight safe checkpoints and exit
  - feature-flag behind runtime.enable_cooperative_shutdown
- migrate Redis client from Jedis blocking calls to Lettuce/reactive client for async XREADGROUP/XCLAIM flows
- upgrade kafka-clients to 3.5.x and replace any blocking poll-with-timeout hotspots with non-blocking reactive wrappers where feasible
- add end-to-end tests: partition hot-spot simulation, coordinated shutdown integration test, retry-storm regression test
- dashboards and alerts: a Grafana board for limiter metrics and a PagerDuty alert if hard_reject_count spikes > 1% over 1m

Design trade-offs and decisions made so far:
- Chose token-bucket per-partition instead of credit-based scheduler to keep implementation deterministic and easy to reason about for ops. Token refill uses workload-aware rate suggestions from Optimize service later (out of scope for this ticket).
- Cooperative shutdown is best-effort: Redis consumer groups and Kafka rebalances are inherently eventually consistent. We implement fast-path XCLAIM + rebalance sync but still include a timed fallback to avoid long drains during network partitions.
- We will not attempt tenant auto-resizing in this ticket; capacity knobs remain config-driven.

Acceptance criteria (must satisfy all):
- PartitionInflightLimiter implemented and exercised by unit tests
- Worker shutdown implements cooperative handshake and falls back to timed drain; integration test demonstrates reduced retry volume vs current baseline (>= 60% reduction in induced retries in test harness)
- All blocking Redis/Kafka calls on worker hot paths converted to async/reactive APIs; no blocking calls in core worker request path (validated by thread-dump checks in CI)
- Metrics emitted and Grafana dashboard created; alert rule authored in perf-oncall folder
- PRs reviewed and merged; canary rollout plan listed and feature-flag gating present

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag behind runtime.enable_cooperative_shutdown default false
2) Merge and run canary on staging cluster with synthetic workload (partition-hotspot test) for 48h
3) Enable on 5% of production worker pool with aggressive monitoring for 1h
4) Ramp to 25% if no regressions, then 100% over 24h
5) If hard_reject_count > 0.5% or request latency regresses > 20% for 5m, rollback feature flag

Open questions / Risks:
- Some legacy integrations expect immediate ack semantics; forced timed drain may cause duplicate processing beyond retries tracked by our idempotency layer. Need to confirm idempotency coverage for high-throughput tenants.
- Upgrading kafka-clients may require version alignment with other services (coordination with infra).
- XCLAIM semantics vary by Redis version; we must pin supported Redis minor versions in runtime-2.3 release notes.
